version: Omega Path Algebra Hard Tests v1.4
formal_results_with_short_proofs: No zero divisors: if A and B are nonempty path multisets, choose a path a in A and b in B; then a concatenated with b occurs in A⊗B, so A⊗B is nonempty.
The structural zero is not a physical nothingness claim; it is the additive identity in this algebraic representation.
The singleton empty path is a multiplicative identity.
No nonzero additive inverses exist with nonnegative multiplicities, so the structure is not a ring.
Naive structural-prime theory under plain path concatenation is mostly trivial: every singleton path of length >1 factors at every internal cut.
decision_on_structural_primes: REJECT naive prime-number analogy for the current path product. It adds little because ordinary path length already determines many factorizations. Revisit only if a richer multiplication produces nontrivial irreducibles.
cancellation_status: Extensive random and exhaustive-small tests found no cancellation failure; a formal proof should use a fixed admissible word order/leading term argument before publication.
